issues.legal_issue: A local council member who continues to reside on government or public land encroached upon by another person is treated as an encroacher and is disqualified from continuing as a member.
material_facts: The appellant was an elected member of a Gram Panchayat.
Her father-in-law and husband had encroached on government land and had not vacated it despite notices.
The appellant was using the encroached land, and the concurrent factual findings that the encroachment continued were upheld.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was disqualified because her continued use and occupation of the encroached land made her a continuing encroacher, although the initial encroachment was by her relatives. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(j-3) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayat Act, 1958 disqualifies a person who has encroached on government land or public property. Reading that provision purposively in the context of Sections 10, 11, 53(1), 53(2), 53(2-A) and 184, continued residence on or occupation of encroached public property amounts to continued encroachment and creates a conflict of interest with a member’s duties. The Court relied on the approach in Devidas Surwade, Sandip Ganpatrao Bhadade and Anita Laxman Junghare, and held that Sagar Pandurang Dhundare stated the law incorrectly and overruled it.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_member_disqualification and elected_local_council_member and public_property_is_encroached and member_continues_to_reside_there

predicates.appeal_challenging_member_disqualificati: A person appealed a decision disqualifying a local council member.
predicates.elected_local_council_member: The person whose disqualification is challenged was elected to a local council.
predicates.public_property_is_encroached: Government or public property was being occupied without authorization.
predicates.member_continues_to_reside_there: The member continued to reside on or occupy the encroached property.
predicates.member_is_disqualified_for_continued_enc: The member is disqualified because the continued residence or occupation constitutes encroachment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the disqualification of an elected local council member who continues to reside on encroached public property, the member is disqualified for continued encroachment.
